From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acme-corp.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2027 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Embeddings model fit & validation — post-call recap & next steps

Looping in a short preliminary validation note after a quick run on the sample you shared (thanks for the fast turnaround). Attached: embeddings_benchmark_results.csv and prompt_set_v1.txt (examples we used). High-level:

Data used:
- ~10,200 queries (mix of support/search)
- ~24,800 candidate docs (product pages + transcripts)
- ~520 labeled query->doc relevance pairs for metric calculation

Models evaluated:
- redwood-embed-large-v1 (1536d) — our internal large embedding tuned for semantic search
- open-embed-1024 (1024d) — baseline open model

Key metrics (preliminary):
- redwood-embed-large-v1: recall@10 = 0.78, MRR = 0.62, avg cosine sim (pos pairs) = 0.71
- open-embed-1024: recall@10 = 0.65, MRR = 0.49, avg cosine sim (pos pairs) = 0.59
- Index size (annoy/faiss approximation): redwood (1536d) ~ 4.5GB, open-embed (1024d) ~ 3.1GB

Drift / distribution notes:
- We computed average cosine drift between last-quarter (Q4) queries and the current sample: mean Δcosine = 0.12 (magnitude indicates moderate drift).
- K-L divergence on top-terms embedding projection suggests the recent product SKUs introduce a distinct cluster; silhouette coefficient increased from 0.08->0.21 which aligns with new-subdomain formation.

Quality regression risk:
- Red flags: when we downsample to short-form queries (<8 tokens), the recall delta shrinks (~0.05 gap), which suggests the larger model gains more on longer-context queries.
- Quantization: 8-bit quantization showed negligible metric drop for redwood-embed-large-v1 in our quick test (~1-2% relative), which is promising for cost/latency tradeoffs.

Recommendations / next steps:
1) Run full evaluation (same metrics + latency p95/p90 in your thin-client environment) on the full 25k candidate corpus. Estimated run: 2 business days.
2) If latency is an issue, test redwood-embed-large-v1 with 8-bit quantization and batched retrieval (we can provide config).
3) Add weekly / rolling drift checks: simple cosine-prototype drift and monthly reindexing trigger if average Δcosine > 0.08.
4) Tune similarity threshold per-query-type (support vs product search) using the labeled set — we'll produce suggested per-type thresholds.

Attachments: embeddings_benchmark_results.csv (metrics + per-query breakdown), prompt_set_v1.txt (query templates used for synthetic tests)

I'll prepare a short slide with key visuals for the Tue review. LMK if you want additional metrics (AUC, recall@1/5) in advance.

Best,
Marissa Cole
